correctness.rationale: For the three-square rows, Gauss's class-number formula and genus theory force r_3(n)/8 to be even for every square-free composite in the relevant mod-8 classes, while the source proves oddness for primes. For the x^2+3y^2+5z^2 rows, a sign-orbit parity reduction plus exact representation multiplicities for the discriminants -12 and -60 gives composite evenness, including the separate 3m branch in the modulus-40 row. The result is also checked by exact integer enumeration through 100000, and explicit outside-row counterexamples confirm the scope is not being overgeneralized.

originality.rationale: Im--Shin Proposition 7.1 gives the all-index coefficient congruences, but their parity lemmas and resulting theorem treat prime indices. Classical genus theory and binary-form representation facts supply the ingredients here, but searches found no statement synthesizing them into the prime-indicator parity law on all twelve comparison rows or the resulting one-extra-(1+i) divisibility for every square-free composite. The motivating preprint is extremely recent, so unindexed contemporaneous work remains the main residual risk.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies a sharp structural limit of the published prime argument: its first mod-(1+i) comparison layer is exactly a primality detector on the relevant square-free progressions and therefore cannot certify any composite nonvanishing there. This rules out a natural extension route and isolates the genuinely new information required for composite results: higher (1+i)-adic data, different comparators, or direct Fourier-coefficient analysis.
